title: Ambient pin scope, environment overrides, and resolution precedence for SDK/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a clear, environment-aware pin resolution contract for the SDK and public API so that applications can deterministically pin model versions using tag, semver (exact and range), or commit hashes while supporting scoped/environment overrides (team/region) and runtime fallbacks.
background: Customers request deterministic control over model versions for reproducibility and rollback. Current behavior is inconsistent across SDKs and runtime: some clients treat tags as highest priority, others prefer semver ranges, and there is no documented mechanism to let a runtime or deployment environment override pins for temporary patching (e.g., replace 'stable' in us-east with a hotfix). This leads to surprising rollouts and operational complexity.
proposal_summary: Introduce an explicit, documented precedence for pin resolution and add 'ambient' scope overrides for environments and tenants. Resolution order (highest -> lowest): 1) explicit immutable ref (commit hash / ABI hash), 2) exact semver pin (e.g., 1.2.3), 3) semver ranges with constraints (e.g., ^1.2), 4) environment-scoped override (env/team/region-level pin), 5) curated tags (e.g., 'stable', 'recommended'), 6) mutable aliases (e.g., 'latest'), 7) runtime fallback mapping (compatible model variants). SDKs will expose this order and a small opt-in API to supply an ambient override at client init or via configuration. The runtime will honor overrides from a policy file and expose a clear audit trail when overrides are applied.
api_examples:
Example 1 - explicit hash pin:
{
  "model": "openlm/text-3",
  "pin": "sha256:9f1a..."
}
Example 2 - semver range with env override (client):
client = RedwoodClient(config={ 'env': 'staging', 'ambient_pins': { 'openlm/text-3': '1.2.x' } })
client.predict({ 'model': 'openlm/text-3', 'pin': '^1.2' })
Example 3 - no pin -> server applies tagged pin:
client.predict({ 'model': 'openlm/text-3' })  // server routes to tag 'stable' unless an env override exists
tradeoffs: Pros: deterministic behavior, safe emergency patching via env overrides, auditable decisions. Cons: increased surface area (new ambient config APIs), potential confusion if customers rely on implicit 'latest' behavior. To mitigate, ambient overrides are opt-in and clearly logged; SDK defaults remain conservative (no ambient overrides unless configured).
compatibility_notes: We will preserve existing default behavior for clients that do not opt into ambient overrides. For old SDKs that pass a simple tag like 'stable', the runtime mapping for 'stable' remains but will be documented. Migration docs will recommend explicit semver pins for reproducibility. A compatibility shim will translate legacy alias pins to the new precedence with a warning log in the runtime for at least one release cycle.
rollout_plan: 1) Spec PR and design doc review (confluence + RFC) - 1 sprint. 2) SDK surface: add ambient override config + logging (alpha SDK release). 3) Runtime: policy file support + audit logs + flag to enable enforcement. 4) Integration tests and canary cluster with a handful of internal services. 5) Beta to selected customers, collect feedback. 6) GA with migration guidance and expanded docs. Feature-flag the strict enforcement until GA.
acceptance_criteria: SDK surface added: ambient_pins config accepted on client init and via environment variable
Resolution order implemented in SDK and runtime matches documented precedence and has unit tests for each step
Runtime emits structured audit entries when an env override is applied (trace id + resolved pin source)
Compatibility shim logs at least one warning for legacy alias use when the new precedence would change routing
Integration canary shows zero user-visible regressions for pinned traffic and expected steering for env overrides
API docs and migration guide published in confluence + SDK changelog entry
testing_notes: Unit tests for precedence permutations, property-based tests for semver ranges, integration tests across SDKs (python/node/go) that simulate env override policies, canary with synthetic load to validate performance and fallbacks. Add observability checks to confirm routing decisions (per-request metadata).
